chunk_findings.detail: The shipped catalog declares two family tables, `[REDACTED:host]` and `family.unknown`, but both contain only a `note` and no `identity`, `src`, or `d`. The stated invariant/test for this change is that every family has source and date, so a validator/test that iterates all `[family.*]` tables will reject the shipped catalog at these two rows; if they are meant to be exempt, the catalog still violates the manifest’s “every family has source and date” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/families.toml:[REDACTED:host]

chunk_findings.detail: The catalog treats `price_out` as a price fact (it records one for `[REDACTED:host]` at line 34), but the paid model entries `model.deepseek-flash` and `model.deepseek-v4-pro` omit it. A non-local route serving `deepseek-flash` therefore has a non-zero input price but no output price; a cost/limit calculation that sums input and output token costs cannot include output cost. If the loader treats a missing price fact as zero, output tokens are silently billed at $0; if it requires all price facts for a priced model, the route is rejected even though the catalog advertises the model. The comment on line 15 admits the omission rather than recording an explicit unknown or blocking non-local pricing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/models.toml:16

chunk_findings.detail: The route is declared `class = "saas"` even though its endpoint is a loopback proxy that ddflow launches (`base_url = "http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:4000/v1"` and `launch.command = "litellm --model {model} --port 4000"`). The file’s own header states that a route whose class is `local` is the one whose address is a tool’s documented local port and that such routes use the zero per-token `[REDACTED:host]` price facts. Given a call through `litellm` to a local model such as `qwen3:8b`, the catalog will classify the route as SaaS rather than local, so the zero local-cost facts are not applied; the run treats a local proxy call as a paid SaaS call (or, if class gates launching, the `launch` command is not used and the proxy is never started).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes.toml:87 (`[route.litellm]`)

chunk_findings.detail: `load` overlays a local row with `dict.update`, which merges only the top-level keys. For route rows this means a local `served` table replaces the shipped route’s entire `served` table instead of merging individual served-model facts. Given a shipped `routes.toml` with `[route.x.served.m.window]` and `[route.x.served.other.window]`, and a local `.ddflow/local/models.toml` with `[route.x.served.m.cache]`, after `load` the catalog has only `route.x.served.m.cache`; the shipped `window` fact for `m` and all facts for `other` are silently dropped. `read(cat, "m", "window", route="x")` then returns “not verified” even though the fact exists in the shipped catalog, contradicting the function’s “local row of the same id replaces fact by fact” contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: `resolve` falls through to needle matching when a model row is present but its `family` is not in `cat.family`. That can make a listed model resolve to a neighbouring family by needle, violating “a listed model id … else the first family whose needle …” and “never a nearest neighbour.” For example, if `model.foo.family = "missing"` and family `anthropic` has identity needles `["foo"]`, `resolve(cat, "foo")` returns `anthropic` with `how="needle"` instead of `unknown` or a model-based result. `_link_problems` may later report the missing family, but `resolve` itself silently performs the neighbour match.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:177

chunk_findings.detail: The local-address assertion uses a prefix regex (`re.match(r"http://(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost)[:/]", url)`) instead of parsing the URL, so a committed local route can point to a remote host and still pass. For example, a committed `routes.toml` route with `class = "local"` and `endpoint.v.base_url = "http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:[REDACTED:email]/v1"` is matched by the regex at the beginning of the string, but its actual host is `evil.com`; the test therefore fails to enforce the stated “no remote local address” invariant.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:115

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` family uses the unanchored needle `gpt`. Because family resolution is “first row whose needle the model name contains,” a real non-OpenAI model name such as `gpt-j-6b` (or any other model name containing `gpt`) resolves to family `openai` and vendor `openai`. That is wrong: `gpt-j-6b` is not an OpenAI-vendor model, so the vendor fact used for review independence is incorrect, and the model does not resolve to `unknown` as the intent requires for a model with no matching family. The needle needs to be scoped/anchored or exclusions need to be added.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/families.toml:[family.openai]

chunk_findings.detail: The endpoint value carries the command template `llm -m {model}`, but the same endpoint value has no `model` key. The file’s own contract says the preset includes a default model, and a command template with `{model}` needs one. If a caller uses the preset to build the command from the endpoint value, e.g. `endpoint["v"]["command"].format(**endpoint["v"])`, selecting `llm-cli` without an explicit model raises `KeyError: "model"` or leaves the literal `{model}` in the command, making the shipped default unusable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes.toml:[route.llm-cli]

chunk_findings.detail: The endpoint value includes `launch.command = "litellm --model {model} --port 4000"`, but `endpoint.v` has no `model` default. If the launch command is formatted from the endpoint value as a preset, starting the LiteLLM proxy from this route fails with `KeyError: "model"` or produces an invalid command; the route cannot be launched as shipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes.toml:[route.litellm]

chunk_findings.detail: `_shape_problems` treats `served` as a plain key and never validates that each served model is a table. Given a local `routes.toml` containing `[route.r.served]` with `model = "oops"`, `_shape_problems` emits no problem because `served` is in `_PLAIN_KEYS`; `validate` then calls `_fact_nodes`, which iterates `tbl.items()` with `tbl == "oops"` and raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'`. `validate` is supposed to return problem strings, not crash on malformed local data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:_shape_problems

chunk_findings.detail: `_shape_problems` excludes the reserved keys `family` and `class` from the “is not a fact” check but does not check that their values are strings. Given a model row such as `[model."m"] family = {}` (or `family = []`), `_shape_problems` does not flag it; `_link_problems` then evaluates `row.get("family") not in cat.family`, which raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` (or list). `resolve` has the same failure mode. A malformed local overlay should produce a validation problem, not an exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:_link_problems

chunk_findings.detail: In the cache-family tier, if a fact is readable but `CF.usable(node, model)` returns `None`, the code sets `node = None` and continues without adding a lead. If no other tier has a fact, `read` returns a miss reason ending in `(no fact recorded)` even though a cache-family fact existed but was not usable for that model. This contradicts the stated contract that a miss says why.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:read

chunk_findings.detail: The “no keys” assertion only looks for `sk-` or `Bearer ` followed by 8+ alphanumeric characters. A committed TOML file can still contain a credential that the test misses. For example, `api_key = [REDACTED] matches no `sk-`/`Bearer` prefix, and Anthropic-style keys such as `api_key = [REDACTED] also miss the regex because only `ant` (3 alphanumeric characters) follows `sk-` before a hyphen. In either case `test_committed_files_hold_no_keys_and_no_remote_local_address` passes even though the committed file contains a secret, so the test does not enforce the invariant it claims to check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:111

chunk_findings.detail: The shipped catalog declares `[[REDACTED:host]]` and `[family.unknown]` as family rows, but each contains only `note` and no `identity` fact with `src` and `d`. The change’s stated invariant/test is that every family has source and date, and `family.unknown` is explicitly the family used when no other family matches. Loading the shipped `families.toml` therefore yields family entries without provenance; a test or validator that enumerates all `[family.*]` tables (as `test_every_family_has_source_and_date` must do to enforce the stated invariant) will fail/reject the shipped catalog. If these rows are intended to be exempt, the shipped data still does not satisfy the manifest’s “every family has source and date” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/families.toml:67

chunk_findings.detail: The file treats `price_out` as a catalogued price fact (`[[REDACTED:host]].price_out`, line 35) and records `max_output` for the paid DeepSeek models, but neither paid model row contains a `price_out` fact. For a non-local route serving `deepseek-flash`, the catalog therefore has a non-zero input/cache price and an output-token limit, but no output price. A cost/limit calculation that needs the output price cannot include it; if it sums the price facts it knows, it returns a total that silently omits output cost, and if it requires a complete paid-model price set it fails. The added comment “The output price was not recorded there: left out” records the omission but does not make the paid-model price data complete.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/models.toml:17 (`model.deepseek-flash`, and similarly `model.deepseek-v4-pro`)

chunk_findings.detail: The route sets `base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1"` while declaring `kind = "anthropic"`. With the official Anthropic SDK/client implied by that kind, `base_url` is the API root and the client appends `/v1/messages`; passing this value makes the request URL `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/v1/messages`. Thus any call routed through `[route.anthropic]`, e.g. the default model `claude-sonnet-5`, will fail with a 404/unknown path. The SDK base URL should be `https://api.anthropic.com`, or the field must be documented/used as a full versioned prefix rather than an SDK `base_url`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes.toml:[route.anthropic]

chunk_findings.detail: `_merge_row` assumes every value under `served` is a mapping before calling `.update()` on it, but `_row_problem` explicitly treats a non-table `served` model value as a validation problem. Given a shipped route row that already has `[route.x.served.m.window]` and a local `.ddflow/local/models.toml` containing `[route.x.served]` with `m = 1`, `load` executes `into["served"].setdefault("m", {}).update(1)` and raises `TypeError` (or `ValueError` for a string value), so the catalog cannot be loaded and `validate` never gets to report the malformed row. The same malformed `served` value added only by the local overlay, when the shipped route has no `served` table so `_merge_row` stores it unchanged, then makes `read`/`_tiers` crash at `(r.get("served") or {}).get(res.model)` or `_tier(served, key)` with `AttributeError`. A malformed user overlay should be a validation problem, not an unhandled exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:_merge_row

chunk_findings.detail: The secret-scan assertion rejects valid catalog data. The pattern `^\s*\w*(key|token|secret)\w*\s*=\s*"[^"]{8,}"` matches any key containing `key`, including `api_key_env`, and the preceding `text.replace("_env", "")` does not prevent that; for a committed route entry such as `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"`, the line still matches the forbidden pattern after replacement (`api_key = [REDACTED] so the test fails even though the value is only an environment-variable name, not a literal key.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: `resolve` consumes `ident.get("needles", [])` and calls `n.lower()` without checking that the identity value is a list of strings. `_identity_problem` only reports this malformed shape through `validate`; `load` and `read` do not run that check first. Given a local overlay such as `[family.openai.identity.v] needles = [1]`, `resolve(cat, "foo")` reaches `any(n and n.lower() in low for n in ident.get("needles", []))`, and `1.lower()` raises `AttributeError`. Since `read` calls `resolve`, a malformed local fact can crash catalog reads instead of producing the validation problem the module otherwise describes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:resolve

chunk_findings.detail: `load` assumes each top-level table and `sources` is a mapping. A git-ignored local file `.ddflow/local/models.toml` containing valid TOML such as `model = "oops"` reaches `for rid, row in (doc.get(table) or {}).items()` and raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'`; an array of tables like `[[model]]` also crashes. Thus malformed local overlay data can prevent `validate` from ever returning a problem, contrary to the module’s pattern of retaining malformed rows so validation can report them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` only checks that `endpoint` is a fact; it never validates that `endpoint.v` is a table, while `presets` silently skips any route whose `v` is not a dict. Given a route row such as `[route.r.endpoint]` with `s = "unverified"`, `v = "http://localhost:4000"`, `source = "x"`, and `d = "2026-01-01"`, `validate` returns no problem, but `presets(cat)` omits `r` entirely. A route that appears valid in the catalog therefore disappears from the rebuilt review presets.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:presets

chunk_findings.detail: The “no keys” check converts every `*_env` assignment into a key-like assignment and then treats any quoted value of 8+ characters as a secret. A valid environment-variable reference such as `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` is not a committed credential, but after `text.replace("_env", "")` it becomes `api_key = [REDACTED] and matches the regex, causing the test to fail on legitimate shipped or local route data. The test should exempt `*_env` values or only flag values that actually look like secrets.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:112

The change’s stated invariant/test is that every family has source and date, and `family.unknown` is explicitly the family used when no other family matches. Loading the shipped `families.toml` therefore yields family entries without provenance; a test or validator that enumerates all `[family.*]` tables (as `test_every_family_has_source_and_date` must do to enforce the stated invariant) will fail/reject the shipped catalog. If these rows are intended to be exempt, the shipped data still does not satisfy the manifest’s “every family has source and date” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/families.toml:67

chunk_findings.detail: The file treats `price_out` as a catalogued price fact (`[[REDACTED:host]].price_out`, line 35) and records `max_output` for the paid DeepSeek models, but neither paid model row contains a `price_out` fact. For a non-local route serving `deepseek-flash`, the catalog therefore has a non-zero input/cache price and an output-token limit, but no output price. A cost/limit calculation that needs the output price cannot include it; if it sums the price facts it knows, it returns a total that silently omits output cost, and if it requires a complete paid-model price set it fails. The added comment “The output price was not recorded there: left out” records the omission but does not make the paid-model price data complete.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/models.toml:17 (`model.deepseek-flash`, and similarly `model.deepseek-v4-pro`)

chunk_findings.detail: The route sets `base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1"` while declaring `kind = "anthropic"`. With the official Anthropic SDK/client implied by that kind, `base_url` is the API root and the client appends `/v1/messages`; passing this value makes the request URL `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/v1/messages`. Thus any call routed through `[route.anthropic]`, e.g. the default model `claude-sonnet-5`, will fail with a 404/unknown path. The SDK base URL should be `https://api.anthropic.com`, or the field must be documented/used as a full versioned prefix rather than an SDK `base_url`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes.toml:[route.anthropic]

chunk_findings.detail: `_merge_row` assumes every value under `served` is a mapping before calling `.update()` on it, but `_row_problem` explicitly treats a non-table `served` model value as a validation problem. Given a shipped route row that already has `[route.x.served.m.window]` and a local `.ddflow/local/models.toml` containing `[route.x.served]` with `m = 1`, `load` executes `into["served"].setdefault("m", {}).update(1)` and raises `TypeError` (or `ValueError` for a string value), so the catalog cannot be loaded and `validate` never gets to report the malformed row. The same malformed `served` value added only by the local overlay, when the shipped route has no `served` table so `_merge_row` stores it unchanged, then makes `read`/`_tiers` crash at `(r.get("served") or {}).get(res.model)` or `_tier(served, key)` with `AttributeError`. A malformed user overlay should be a validation problem, not an unhandled exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:_merge_row

chunk_findings.detail: The secret-scan assertion rejects valid catalog data. The pattern `^\s*\w*(key|token|secret)\w*\s*=\s*"[^"]{8,}"` matches any key containing `key`, including `api_key_env`, and the preceding `text.replace("_env", "")` does not prevent that; for a committed route entry such as `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"`, the line still matches the forbidden pattern after replacement (`api_key = [REDACTED] so the test fails even though the value is only an environment-variable name, not a literal key.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: The new malformed-table reporting misses falsy non-table top-level values. If a local overlay contains `family = []` (or `family = 0`, `family = false`, `family = ""`), `doc.get("family") or {}` yields `{}`, so the `not isinstance(rows, dict)` branch is never taken and no `bad_rows` entry is added. Given a committed family such as `[family.foo]` with an identity needle matching `gpt`, loading a local `models.toml` containing only `family = []` leaves `family.foo` in the catalog and makes `validate(cat)` return no problems, even though the local table is malformed and, under the new contract, should be kept out and reported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:load (`rows = doc.get(table) or {}`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` family still matches on the unanchored substring `gpt`, so a model name that merely contains `gpt` resolves to family `openai` with vendor `openai`. Given a model name such as `gpt-j-6b`, the first matching family row is `openai`, not `unknown`, even though GPT-J is not an OpenAI-vendor model. This makes the vendor fact used for review independence incorrect and violates the intent that a model with no real family match resolves to `unknown`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/families.toml:23

chunk_findings.detail: `resolve` consumes `ident.get("needles", [])` and calls `n.lower()` without checking that the identity value is a list of strings. `_identity_problem` only reports this malformed shape through `validate`; `load` and `read` do not run that check first. Given a local overlay such as `[family.openai.identity.v] needles = [1]`, `resolve(cat, "foo")` reaches `any(n and n.lower() in low for n in ident.get("needles", []))`, and `1.lower()` raises `AttributeError`. Since `read` calls `resolve`, a malformed local fact can crash catalog reads instead of producing the validation problem the module otherwise describes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:resolve

chunk_findings.detail: `load` assumes each top-level table and `sources` is a mapping. A git-ignored local file `.ddflow/local/models.toml` containing valid TOML such as `model = "oops"` reaches `for rid, row in (doc.get(table) or {}).items()` and raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'`; an array of tables like `[[model]]` also crashes. Thus malformed local overlay data can prevent `validate` from ever returning a problem, contrary to the module’s pattern of retaining malformed rows so validation can report them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` only checks that `endpoint` is a fact; it never validates that `endpoint.v` is a table, while `presets` silently skips any route whose `v` is not a dict. Given a route row such as `[route.r.endpoint]` with `s = "unverified"`, `v = "http://localhost:4000"`, `source = "x"`, and `d = "2026-01-01"`, `validate` returns no problem, but `presets(cat)` omits `r` entirely. A route that appears valid in the catalog therefore disappears from the rebuilt review presets.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:presets

chunk_findings.detail: The “no keys” check converts every `*_env` assignment into a key-like assignment and then treats any quoted value of 8+ characters as a secret. A valid environment-variable reference such as `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` is not a committed credential, but after `text.replace("_env", "")` it becomes `api_key = [REDACTED] and matches the regex, causing the test to fail on legitimate shipped or local route data. The test should exempt `*_env` values or only flag values that actually look like secrets.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_catalog.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: A non-mapping `sources` table is still silently dropped. Given a local `.ddflow/local/models.toml` containing only `sources = 3` (or `sources = []`), `load` evaluates `isinstance(doc.get("sources"), dict)`, skips the update, and does not add anything to `cat.bad_rows`; `validate(cat)` therefore returns no problem for that malformed top-level table. This is the remaining part of the earlier `sources` concern: non-table `family/model/route/cls` are now reported, but invalid `sources` data is accepted without validation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/modelreg.py:load
